extracted.intended_audience: students/readers of commutative algebra (e.g., Atiyah–MacDonald) — advanced undergraduates or graduate students working through exercises
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions, hints, and commentary for exercises/theorems about primary decomposition, associated primes, symbolic powers, and related module-level analogues in commutative algebra. Aimed at mastering detection/construction of primary decompositions and properties of primes/primary ideals and modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 47: PP rings are absolutely flat
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a ring. If all the primary ideals of A are prime, then A is absolutely flat. (Define PP = property that all primary ideals are prime.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: reduce to showing each local PP ring is a field; property inherited by quotients and localizations. Consider cases (1) m is only prime ideal, (2) A domain with minimal prime over (a) in m, (3) general domain case choosing a nonzero a in m and minimal prime over (a), and (4) general case using a prime p< m and reduction to previous cases. Use results from Section 4.2.10 and Nakayama's Lemma as cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.4: example of m-primary not a power
rubrics_metrics.description: In Z[t], m = (2, t) is maximal and q = (4, t) is m-primary, but q is not a power of m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Z[t]/q ≅ Z/4Z, and note the strict containment m^2 < q < m (so q is between m^2 and m). This exhibits an m-primary ideal that is not a pure power of m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.5: primary decomposition for product of primes
rubrics_metrics.description: In K[x,y,z], with p1=(x,y), p2=(x,z), m=(x,y,z), let a = p1 p2. Show a = p1 ∩ p2 ∩ m^2 is a reduced primary decomposition. Identify isolated vs embedded components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that ideals generated by monomials have the property that f ∈ a iff all monomials of f are in a; intersections and products of monomial ideals stay monomial-generated. For a variant algebra with relations (x^2=xy=...), explicit decompositions of graded pieces are given: A = K ⊕ Kx ⊕ yK[y] ⊕ zK[z], etc., and compute intersections p1∩p2 = Kx, p1∩m^2 = y^2K[y], p2∩m^2 = z^2K[z].

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.6: decomposability of (0) in C(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be infinite compact Hausdorff, A=C(X) real-valued continuous functions. Is the zero ideal decomposable in A?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim: any prime ideal is contained in a unique maximal ideal. Using Urysohn's Lemma produce functions f,g with fg=0 distinguishing two maximal ideals mx,my, showing uniqueness. Conclude there are infinitely many minimal prime ideals, so (0) is not decomposable as a finite intersection of primary ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.7: extension of ideals to polynomial ring A[x]
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) For ideal a in A, a[x] is its extension in A[x]. (ii) If p ⊂ A is prime then p[x] ⊂ A[x] is prime. (iii) If q is p-primary in A then q[x] is p[x]-primary in A[x]. (iv) If a = ∩_{i=1}^n q_i minimal primary decomposition in A then a[x] = ∩ q_i[x] is minimal primary decomposition in A[x]. (v) If p minimal prime of a then p[x] minimal prime of a[x].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that A[x] is faithfully flat over A. Lemma 48: fiber of Spec(A[x])→Spec(A) over p ≅ Spec(k[x]) (k residue field at p); least element is p[x] and p[x]+(x) is maximal in the fiber. Use exercises and results in earlier sections as cited to prove parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 48 (fiber lemma for A→A[x])
rubrics_metrics.description: For f:A→A[x] embedding, fiber f^*^{-1}(p) over prime p is order-isomorphic to Spec(k[x]) where k is residue field at p. The least element of the fiber is p[x], and p[x]+(x) is a maximal element of the fiber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prove behavior of primes and minimal primes under extension to polynomial rings; consult Exercises 3.21iv and Section 4.2.21 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.8: canonical primes in polynomial ring
rubrics_metrics.description: In k[x1,...,xn], the ideals p_i = (x1,...,xi) are prime (1≤i≤n) and all their powers are primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reduction splitting variables: set B = k[x1,...,xr], A = B[y1,...,ys], m=(x1,...,xr) ⊂ B, p = (x1,...,xr) ⊂ A; show p^n = m^n [y1,...,ys] and use Exercise 4.7(iii) to deduce p^n is p-primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.9: the set D(A) and zero-divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Define D(A) = {prime ideals p: ∃a with p minimal among primes containing (0:a)}. (a) b ∈ A is a zero-divisor iff b ∈ p for some p ∈ D(A). (b) For multiplicative S, D(S^{-1}A) = S^{-1}D(A). (c) If (0) has a primary decomposition, then D(A) equals the set of associated prime ideals of (0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs: (a) show b in some p minimal over (0:a) ⇔ b zero-divisor via constructing multiplicative set T={b^n s | n∈N, s∉p} and prime containing (0:a) disjoint from T; converse uses Prop 1.15. (b) reduce to equivalent statements about minimality after localization. (c) use uniqueness theorem expressing minimal primes over (0:a) as r(0:a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.10: properties of Sp(0) (kernel of A→A_p)
rubrics_metrics.description: For prime p, let S_p(0) = ker(A→A_p). (i) S_p(0) ⊂ p. (ii) p minimal prime ⇔ r_A(S_p(0)) = p. (iii) p ⊃ p' ⇒ S_p(0) ⊂ S_{p'}(0). (iv) For 0 ≠ a ∈ A there exists p minimal over (0:a) and hence a ∉ S_p(0). Also S_p(0) = ⋂_{s∈A ackslash p} (0:s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express S_p(0) as contraction (0)^c. Use equality r_A(S_p(0)) = (r_{A_p}(0))^c and properties of radicals in localizations. Use existence of primes minimal over annihilators for (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.11: Sp(0) is smallest p-primary ideal and relation to nilradical
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If p is minimal prime, Sp(0) is the smallest p-primary ideal. (b) Let a be intersection of Sp(0) over minimal primes; then a is contained in nilradical. (c) If (0) is decomposable, then a=(0) iff every prime ideal of (0) is isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that in Ap the nilradical equals unique prime ideal pp and Proposition 4.2: if r(a) maximal then a is primary. For (c) use second uniqueness theorem and structure of reduced decomposition to compare intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.12: saturation S(a) and its properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiplicative S and ideal a, S(a) is contraction of S^{-1}a; show (i) S(a)∩S(b)=S(a∩b). (ii) S(r(a)) = r(S(a)). (iii) S(a) = (1) ⇔ a meets S. (iv) S1(S2(a)) = (S1S2)(a). If a has a primary decomposition, the set {S(a) | S multiplicative} is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow from results on localization and contraction (Propositions and exercises cited: 1.18, 3.11ii/v, 4.9). For finiteness use primary decomposition structure and behavior under localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.13: symbolic powers p^{(n)}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define p^{(n)} = S_p(p^n) where S_p = A ackslash p. Show (i) p^{(n)} is p-primary. (ii) If p^n has a primary decomposition then p^{(n)} is its p-primary component. (iii) If p^{(m)} p^{(n)} has a primary decomposition then p^{(m+n)} is its p-primary component. (iv) p^{(n)} = p^n ⇔ p^n is p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in localization Ap where pp is maximal; powers of maximal ideals are primary (Prop 49). Use claims: (a) if a⊂p with ap = p^k then p^{(k)} is smallest p-primary containing a, (b) with r(a)=p and a has primary decomposition then p^{(k)} is p-primary component. Use contraction arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.14: maximal (a:x) yields prime in a
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decomposable ideal and p is a maximal element among ideals of the form (a:x) with x∉a, then p is prime and belongs to a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: suppose (a:x) not prime, pick y,z violating primality; deduce contradiction to maximality using relations (a:xz) ⊃ (a:x). Use Corollary 40 linked to First Uniqueness Theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.15: constructing isolated component via saturation
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a decomposable with isolated set Σ of prime ideals belonging to a and q_Σ intersection of corresponding primary components. Given f with f∈p ⇔ p∉Σ for primes belonging to a, let S_f = powers of f. Show q_Σ = S_f(a) = (a:f^n) for large n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a = ∩ q_i minimal decomposition, partition indices so Σ={p1..pm}. Use equality S_f(a)=∪_{k≥0} (a:f^k) and compute (a:f^k) = ∩ (q_i : f^k). For i≤m (qi:f^k)=qi; for others (qi: f^k)=(1) for k large. Conclude equality for large k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.16: localization preserves decomposability
rubrics_metrics.description: If every ideal of A has a primary decomposition, then every localization S^{-1}A also has the property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from earlier propositions on contraction/extension of primary decompositions under localization (Prop 3.11i and Prop 4.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.17: condition (L1) implies all ideals are intersections of primary ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume (L1): for every ideal a≠(1) and prime p there exists x∉p with S_p(a) = (a:x). Then every ideal in A is an intersection (possibly infinite) of primary ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct admissible quadruples (b,p,q,x) with q = S_p(b) and q p-primary; use transfinite induction on ordinals to build an increasing chain a_α with Condition C(α): a = a_α ∩ ⋂_{β<α} q_β. Lemmas: existence of admissible quadruples, b = q ∩ (b+(x)), and q primary. The eventual contradiction from assuming a proper closure leads to the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 50 / Lemma 51 (admissible quadruples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissible quadruple (b,p,q,x) where b≠(1), p minimal prime over b, q = S_p(b), x∉p with q=(b:x). Lemma: (a) such exist for any b≠(1); (b) q is p-primary and b = q ∩ (b+(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the transfinite construction: (b:(x)) relations, and Proposition 3.11ii for containment relations of (b:s) across s∉p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.18: equivalence of L1+L2 with decomposability
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition (L2): for descending chain S1⊃S2⊃... of multiplicative subsets, ∃n with S_n(a) = S_{n+1}(a)=... . Show (i) Every ideal has primary decomposition ⇔ (ii) A satisfies (L1) and (L2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: (i)⇒(L1),(L2) via primary decomposition and Prop 4.9. For (ii)⇒(i) use the transfinite construction from Exercise 4.17, let ζ be stopping ordinal; show ζ finite via analysis of Sn and application of (L2) and Lemma 54 (monotonicity of q0∩...∩qn).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.19: intersections of p-primary ideals and existence of ideals with specified associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Every p-primary ideal contains S_p(0) (kernel of A→A_p). (b) If for every p the intersection of all p-primary ideals equals S_p(0) and p1,...,pn are distinct non-minimal primes, then there exists an ideal a whose associated primes are exactly p1,...,pn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) straightforward via contraction of qp in Ap. (b) Induction on n: pick pn maximal among p_i; find b with associated primes p1..p_{n-1}; show b⊄S_{pn}(0) then choose pn-primary qn with b⊂qn; set a=∩ q_i. Includes a corrected proof/attribution to stackexchange user withoutfeather for a reducedness argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.20: radical of a submodule r_M(N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define r_M(N) = {x∈A | x^q M ⊂ N for some q>0}. Show r_M(N) = r((N:M)) = r(Ann(M/N)); hence r_M(N) is an ideal. State analogues of ring radical formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove equalities and analogues: r_A(r_M(N)) = r_M(N); r_M(N∩P)=r_M(N)∩r_M(P); r_M(N)=(1) ⇔ N=M; and inclusion results for sums. Give counterexample to converse inclusion in analogue of (v) using A≠0, M=A⊕A, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.21: primary submodules and (Q:M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define φ_x : m↦xm on M. x is zero-divisor/nilpotent on M by injectivity/nilpotence of φ_x. Q⊂M is primary in M if Q≠M and every zero-divisor in M/Q is nilpotent. Show (Q:M) is a primary ideal; r_M(Q) is prime p and Q is p-primary in M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how replacing q with Q and r with r_M in proofs of (4.3)-(4.4) yields module versions; provide table matching steps to show (Q:M) is primary and other claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.22: primary decomposition of submodules
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary decomposition of submodule N of M is N=∩_{i=1}^n Q_i with Qi primary in M. Minimality requires distinct r_M(Q_i) and no redundant components. Prove prime ideals r_M(Q_i) depend only on N and M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogues of ideal-level uniqueness (4.5) apply: replace qi with Qi and radicals with r_M and follow the same arguments to show prime ideals belonging to N depend only on N and M (equivalently are primes belonging to 0 in M/N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.23: module-level analogues of (4.6)-(4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: State and prove analogues of (4.6)-(4.11) for submodules, particularly properties of zero-divisors in M, localization behavior of p-primary submodules, and correspondence between primary submodules under localization/contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (i) zero-submodule decomposable ⇒ set of zero-divisors of A in M is union of primes belonging to 0⊂M; (ii) localization: if S∩p=∅ and Q p-primary in M then S^{-1}Q is S^{-1}p-primary and contracts back to Q; (iii) use (S^{-1}N : S^{-1}M) containment relations; (iv) adapt proofs from ideal case with table replacing q↦Q and r(q)↦r(Q:M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5.3.21 Bourbaki — associated primes Ass(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and a sequence of lemmas/propositions: Ass(M) = {p | ∃x∈M, Ann(x)=p}. Lemma 56: p associated ⇔ M contains submodule isomorphic to A/p. Prop 57: for nonzero submodule of A/p, Ass = {p}. Prop 58: maximal Ann(x) ideals are prime, hence in Ass(M). Corollaries 59–61 on Ass(M) in noetherian case and zero-divisors. Props 62–70: behavior of Ass under submodules, direct sums, intersections, construction of submodules with prescribed Ass-sets, and Theorem 69 (Muiny): in noetherian rings intersection of primary submodules is 0; more generally N is intersection of primary submodules containing N and can be chosen indexed by Ass(M/N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed structural results for associated primes in the noetherian setting: existence of maximal annihilators, finiteness properties, decomposition into primary submodules with associated primes matching components, and constructive procedures to separate Ass(M) into parts via submodules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on integral extensions and primes (6.1.1–6.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes strengthening Corollary 5.9 and Theorem 5.10: if A⊂B integral and q⊂b ideals of B with qc=bc=p then q=b; contraction of primes and maximal ideals under integral extension; dim A = dim B when B integral over A; integrally closed domain remark (truncated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketches: localize at p, use Proposition 3.11ii to compare bp and Bp; show contraction preserves maximality statements; deduce dimension equalities by combining corollary/theorem results referenced.
